1.text: God, who at sundry times N in divers manners spoke in time past 2 tha fathers by tha prophets,
Has in dese last days spoken 2 us by his Son, whom he has appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made tha worlds;

Who bein tha brightness of his glory, N tha express image of his person, N upholding all things by tha word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on tha right hand of tha Majesty on high;
Bein made so much better than tha angels, as he has by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than dey.
4 2 which of tha angels said he at any time, u r my Son, dis day have I begotten u? N again, I will be 2 him a Father, N he shall be 2 me a Son?
N again, when he brings in tha firstbegotten in2 tha world, he says, N let all tha angels of God worship him.
N of tha angels he says, Who makes his angels spirits, N his ministers a flame of fire.
But 2 tha Son he says, ur throne, O God, is 4 ever N ever: a sceptre of righteousness is tha sceptre of ur kingdom.
u have loved righteousness, N hated iniquity; therefore God, even ur God, has anointed u wit tha oil of gladness above ur fellows.
N, u, Lord, in tha beginning have laid tha foundation of tha earth; N tha heavenz r tha works of thine hands:
Dey shall perish; but u remain; N dey all shall wax old as does a garment;
N as a vesture will u fold ’em up, N dey shall be changed: but u r tha same, N ur years shall not fail.
But 2 which of tha angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine opps ur footstool?
R dey not all ministering spirits, sent forth 2 minister 4 ’em who shall be heirs of salvation?

2.text: Therefore we ought 2 give tha more earnest heed 2 tha things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let ’em slip.
4 if tha word spoken by angels was stedfast, N every transgression N disobedience received a just recompence of reward;
How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at tha first began 2 be spoken by tha Lord, N was confirmed 2 us by ’em dat heard him;
God also bearin ’em witness, both wit signs N wonders, N wit divers miracles, N gifts of tha Holy Ghost, according 2 his own will?
4 2 tha angels has he not put in subjection tha world 2 come, whereof we speak.
But one in a certain place testified, sayin, What is man, dat u r mindful of him? or tha son of man, dat u visitest him?
u made him a little lower than tha angels; u crownedst him wit glory N honour, N did set him over tha works of ur hands:
u have put all things in subjection under his feet. 4 in dat he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing dat is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than tha angels 4 tha sufferin of death, crowned wit glory N honour; dat he by tha grace of God should taste death 4 every man.
4 it became him, 4 whom r all things, N by whom r all things, in bringin many sons 2 glory, 2 make tha captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
4 both he dat sanctifieth N dey who r sanctified r all of one: 4 which cause he is not ashamed 2 call ’em brothers,
Sayin, I will declare ur name 2 my brothers, in tha midst of tha church will I sing praise 2 u.
N again, I will put my trust in him. N again, look I N tha children which God has given me.
Forasmuch then as tha children r partakers of flesh N blood, he also himself likewise took part of tha same; dat through death he might destroy him dat had tha power of death, dat is, tha devil;
N deliver ’em who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject 2 bondage.
4 for real he took not on him tha nature of angels; but he took on him tha seed of Abraham.
So in all things it behoved him 2 be made like 2 his brothers, dat he might be a merciful N faithful high priest in things pertaining 2 God, 2 make reconciliation 4 tha sins of tha people.
4 in dat he himself has suffered bein tempted, he is able 2 succour ’em dat r tempted.

3.text: So, holy brothers, partakers of tha heavenly callin, consider tha Apostle N High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;
Who was faithful 2 him dat appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.
4 dis man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, since as he who has builded tha house has more honour than tha house.
4 every house is builded by some man; but he dat built all things is God.
N Moses for real was faithful in all his house, as a servant, 4 a testimony of dose things which were 2 be spoken after;
But Christ as a son over his own house; whose house r we, if we hold fast tha confidence N tha rejoicin of tha hope firm 2 tha end.
So (as tha Holy Ghost says, 2 day if y’all will hear his voice,
Harden not ur hearts, as in tha provocation, in tha day of temptation in tha wilderness:
When ur fathers tempted me, proved me, N saw my works forty years.
So I was grieved wit dat generation, N said, dey do alway err in their heart; N dey have not known my ways.
So I sware in my wrath, dey shall not enter in2 my rest.)
Pay attention, brothers, lest there be in any of u an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from tha livin God.
But exhort one another daily, while it is called 2 day; lest any of u be hardened through tha deceitfulness of sin.
4 we r made partakers of Christ, if we hold tha beginning of our confidence stedfast 2 tha end;
While it is said, 2 day if y’all will hear his voice, harden not ur hearts, as in tha provocation.
4 some, when dey had heard, did provoke: but not all dat came out of Egypt by Moses.
But wit whom was he grieved forty years? was it not wit ’em dat had sinned, whose carcases fell in tha wilderness?
N 2 whom sware he dat dey should not enter in2 his rest, but 2 ’em dat believed not?
So we see dat dey could not enter in because of unbelief.

4.text: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise bein left us of entering in2 his rest, any of u should seem 2 come short of it.
4 2 us was tha gospel preached, as well as 2 ’em: but tha word preached did not profit ’em, not bein mixed wit faith in ’em dat heard it.
4 we which have believed do enter in2 rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if dey shall enter in2 my rest: although tha works were finished from tha foundation of tha world.
4 he spoke in a certain place of tha seventh day on dis wise, N God did rest tha seventh day from all his works.
N in dis place again, If dey shall enter in2 my rest.
Seein therefore it remains dat some must enter in it, N dey 2 whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief:
Again, he limiteth a certain day, sayin in David, 2 day, after so long a time; as it is said, 2 day if y’all will hear his voice, harden not ur hearts.
4 if Jesus had given ’em rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.
There remains therefore a rest 2 tha people of God.
4 he dat is entered in2 his rest, he also has ceased from his own works, as God did from his.
Let us labour therefore 2 enter in2 dat rest, lest any man fall after tha same example of unbelief.

4 tha word of God is quick, N powerful, N sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even 2 tha dividing asunder of soul N spirit, N of tha joints N marrow, N is a discerner of tha thoughts N intents of tha heart.
Neither is there any creature dat is not manifest in his sight: but all things r naked N opened 2 tha eyes of him wit whom we have 2 do.
Seein then dat we have a great high priest, dat is passed in2 tha heavenz, Jesus tha Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.
4 we have not an high priest which cannot be touched wit tha feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we r, yet without sin.
Let us therefore come boldly 2 tha throne of grace, dat we may obtain mercy, N find grace 2 help in time of need.

5.text: 4 every high priest taken from among men is ordained 4 men in things pertaining 2 God, dat he may offer both gifts N sacrifices 4 sins:
Who can have compassion on tha ignorant, N on ’em dat r out of tha way; 4 dat he himself also is compassed wit infirmity.
N by reason hereof he ought, as 4 tha people, so also 4 himself, 2 offer 4 sins.
N no man takes dis honour 2 himself, but he dat is called of God, as was Aaron.
So also Christ glorified not himself 2 be made an high priest; but he dat said 2 him, u r my Son, 2 day have I begotten u.
As he says also in another place, u r a priest 4 ever after tha order of Melchisedec.
Who in tha days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers N supplications wit strong cryin N tears 2 him dat was able 2 save him from death, N was heard in dat he feared;
Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by tha things which he suffered;
N bein made perfect, he became tha author of eternal salvation 2 all ’em dat obey him;
Called of God an high priest after tha order of Melchisedec.
Of whom we have many things 2 say, N hard 2 be uttered, seein y’all r dull of hearin.
4 when 4 tha time y’all ought 2 be teachers, y’all have need dat one teach u again which be tha first principles of tha oracles of God; N r become such as have need of milk, N not of strong food.
4 every one dat uses milk is unskilful in tha word of righteousness: 4 he is a babe.
But strong food belongs 2 ’em dat r of full age, even dose who by reason of use have their senses exercised 2 discern both good N evil.

6.text: Therefore leavin tha principles of tha doctrine of Christ, let us go on 2 perfection; not laying again tha foundation of repentance from dead works, N of faith toward God,
Of tha doctrine of baptisms, N of laying on of hands, N of resurrection of tha dead, N of eternal judgment.
N dis will we do, if God permit.
4 it is impossible 4 dose who were once enlightened, N have tasted of tha heavenly gift, N were made partakers of tha Holy Ghost,
N have tasted tha good word of God, N tha powers of tha world 2 come,
If dey shall fall away, 2 renew ’em again 2 repentance; seein dey crucify 2 themselves tha Son of God afresh, N put him 2 an open shame.
4 tha earth which drinks in tha rain dat comes oft upon it, N brings forth herbs meet 4 ’em by whom it is dressed, receives blessing from God:
But dat which bears thorns N briers is rejected, N is nigh 2 cursing; whose end is 2 be burned.
But, beloved, we r persuaded better things of u, N things dat accompany salvation, though we like dis speak.
4 God is not unrighteous 2 forget ur work N labour of love, which y’all have showed toward his name, in dat y’all have ministered 2 tha saints, N do minister.
N we desire dat every one of u do show tha same diligence 2 tha full assurance of hope 2 tha end:
Dat y’all don’t be slothful, but followers of ’em who through faith N patience inherit tha promises.
4 when God made promise 2 Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,
Sayin, Surely blessing I will bless u, N multiplying I will multiply u.
N so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained tha promise.
4 men for real swear by tha greater: N an oath 4 confirmation is 2 ’em an end of all strife.
In which God, willin more abundantly 2 show 2 tha heirs of promise tha immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:
Dat by two immutable things, in which it was impossible 4 God 2 lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled 4 refuge 2 lay hold upon tha hope set before us:
Which hope we have as an anchor of tha soul, both sure N stedfast, N which enters in2 dat within tha veil;
Where tha forerunner is 4 us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest 4 ever after tha order of Melchisedec.

7.text: 4 dis Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of tha most high God, who met Abraham returnin from tha slaughter of tha kings, N blessed him;
2 whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first bein by interpretation King of righteousness, N after dat also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;
Without father, without mother, without descent, havin neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like 2 tha Son of God; abides a priest continually.
Now consider how great dis man was, 2 whom even tha patriarch Abraham gave tha tenth of tha spoils.

N for real dey dat r of tha sons of Levi, who receive tha office of tha priesthood, have a commandment 2 take tithes of tha people according 2 tha law, dat is, of their brothers, though dey come out of tha loins of Abraham:
But he whose descent is not counted from ’em received tithes of Abraham, N blessed him dat had tha promises.
N without all contradiction tha less is blessed of tha better.
N here men dat die receive tithes; but there he receives ’em, of whom it is witnessed dat he lives.
N as I may so say, Levi also, who receives tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
4 he was yet in tha loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.

If therefore perfection were by tha Levitical priesthood, (4 under it tha people received tha law,) what further need was there dat another priest should rise after tha order of Melchisedec, N not be called after tha order of Aaron?
4 tha priesthood bein changed, there is made of necessity a change also of tha law.
4 he of whom dese things r spoken pertains 2 another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at tha altar.
4 it is evident dat our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.
N it is yet far more evident: 4 dat after tha similitude of Melchisedec there arises another priest,
Who is made, not after tha law of a carnal commandment, but after tha power of an endless life.
4 he testifieth, u r a priest 4 ever after tha order of Melchisedec.
4 there is for real a disannulling of tha commandment goin before 4 tha weakness N unprofitableness of it.
4 tha law made nothing perfect, but tha bringin in of a better hope did; by tha which we draw nigh 2 God.
N since as not without an oath he was made priest:
(4 dose priests were made without an oath; but dis wit an oath by him dat said 2 him, tha Lord sware N will not repent, u r a priest 4 ever after tha order of Melchisedec:)
By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.
N dey truly were many priests, because dey were not suffered 2 continue by reason of death:
But dis man, because he continueth ever, has an unchangeable priesthood.
So he is able also 2 save ’em 2 tha uttermost dat come 2 God by him, seein he ever lives 2 make intercession 4 ’em.
4 such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, N made higher than tha heavenz;
Who needeth not daily, as dose high priests, 2 offer up sacrifice, first 4 his own sins, N then 4 tha people’s: 4 dis he did once, when he offered up himself.
4 tha law makes men high priests which have infirmity; but tha word of tha oath, which was since tha law, makes tha Son, who is consecrated 4 evermore.

8.text: Now of tha things which we have spoken dis is tha sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on tha right hand of tha throne of tha Majesty in tha heavenz;
A minister of tha sanctuary, N of tha true tabernacle, which tha Lord pitched, N not man.
4 every high priest is ordained 2 offer gifts N sacrifices: so it is of necessity dat dis man have somewhat also 2 offer.
4 if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seein dat there r priests dat offer gifts according 2 tha law:

Who serve 2 tha example N shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about 2 make tha tabernacle: 4, See, says he, dat u make all things according 2 tha pattern showed 2 u in tha mount.
But now has he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is tha mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
4 if dat first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought 4 tha second.
4 finding fault wit ’em, he says, look, tha days come, says tha Lord, when I will make a new covenant wit tha house of Israel N wit tha house of Judah:

Not according 2 tha covenant dat I made wit their fathers in tha day when I took ’em by tha hand 2 lead ’em out of tha land of Egypt; because dey continued not in my covenant, N I regarded ’em not, says tha Lord.

4 dis is tha covenant dat I will make wit tha house of Israel after dose days, says tha Lord; I will put my laws in2 their mind, N write ’em in their hearts: N I will be 2 ’em a God, N dey shall be 2 me a people:
N dey shall not teach every man his neighbour, N every man his brother, sayin, Know tha Lord: 4 all shall know me, from tha least 2 tha greatest.
4 I will be merciful 2 their unrighteousness, N their sins N their iniquities will I remember no more.
In dat he says, A new covenant, he has made tha first old. Now dat which decayeth N grows old is ready 2 vanish away.

9.text: Then for real tha first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, N a worldly sanctuary.
4 there was a tabernacle made; tha first, in which was tha candlestick, N tha table, N tha showbread; which is called tha sanctuary.
N after tha second veil, tha tabernacle which is called tha Holiest of all;
Which had tha golden censer, N tha ark of tha covenant overlaid round about wit gold, in which was tha golden pot dat had manna, N Aaron’s rod dat budded, N tha tables of tha covenant;
N over it tha cherubims of glory shadowing tha mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.
Now when dese things were like dis ordained, tha priests went always in2 tha first tabernacle, accomplishing tha service of God.
But in2 tha second went tha high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered 4 himself, N 4 tha errors of tha people:
Tha Holy Ghost dis signifying, dat tha way in2 tha holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as tha first tabernacle was yet standin:
Which was a figure 4 tha time then present, in which were offered both gifts N sacrifices, dat could not make him dat did tha service perfect, as pertaining 2 tha conscience;
Which stood only in meats N drinks, N divers washings, N carnal ordinances, imposed on ’em until tha time of reformation.
But Christ bein come an high priest of good things 2 come, by a greater N more perfect tabernacle, not made wit hands, dat is 2 say, not of dis buildin;
Neither by tha blood of goats N calves, but by his own blood he entered in once in2 tha holy place, havin obtained eternal redemption 4 us.
4 if tha blood of bulls N of goats, N tha ashes of an heifer sprinkling tha unclean, sanctifieth 2 tha purifying of tha flesh:
How much more shall tha blood of Christ, who through tha eternal Spirit offered himself without spot 2 God, purge ur conscience from dead works 2 serve tha livin God?

N 4 dis cause he is tha mediator of tha new testament, dat by means of death, 4 tha redemption of tha transgressions dat were under tha first testament, dey which r called might receive tha promise of eternal inheritance.
4 where a testament is, there must also of necessity be tha death of tha testator.
4 a testament is of force after men r dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while tha testator lives.
Whereupon neither tha first testament was dedicated without blood.
4 when Moses had spoken every precept 2 all tha people according 2 tha law, he took tha blood of calves N of goats, wit water, N scarlet wool, N hyssop, N sprinkled both tha book, N all tha people,
Sayin, dis is tha blood of tha testament which God has enjoined 2 u.
Moreover he sprinkled wit blood both tha tabernacle, N all tha vessels of tha ministry.
N almost all things r by tha law purged wit blood; N without shedding of blood is no remission.
It was therefore necessary dat tha patterns of things in tha heavenz should be purified wit dese; but tha heavenly things themselves wit better sacrifices than dese.
4 Christ is not entered in2 tha holy places made wit hands, which r tha figures of tha true; but in2 heaven itself, now 2 appear in tha presence of God 4 us:
Nor yet dat he should offer himself often, as tha high priest enters in2 tha holy place every year wit blood of others;
4 then must he often have suffered since tha foundation of tha world: but now once in tha end of tha world has he appeared 2 put away sin by tha sacrifice of himself.
N as it is appointed 2 men once 2 die, but after dis tha judgment:
So Christ was once offered 2 bear tha sins of many; N 2 ’em dat look 4 him shall he appear tha second time without sin 2 salvation.

10.text: 4 tha law havin a shadow of good things 2 come, N not tha very image of tha things, can never wit dose sacrifices which dey offered year by year continually make tha comers thereunto perfect.
4 then would dey not have ceased 2 be offered? because dat tha worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.
But in dose sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
4 it is not possible dat tha blood of bulls N of goats should take away sins.
So when he comes in2 tha world, he says, Sacrifice N offering u would not, but a body have u prepared me:
In burnt offerings N sacrifices 4 sin u have had no pleasure.
Then said I, look, I come (in tha volume of tha book it is written of me,) 2 do ur will, O God.
Above when he said, Sacrifice N offering N burnt offerings N offering 4 sin u would not, neither had pleasure in it; which r offered by tha law;
Then said he, look, I come 2 do ur will, O God. He takes away tha first, dat he may establish tha second.
By tha which will we r sanctified through tha offering of tha body of Jesus Christ once 4 all.
N every priest stands daily ministering N offering oftentimes tha same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:
But dis man, after he had offered one sacrifice 4 sins 4 ever, sat down on tha right hand of God;
From from now on expecting till his opps be made his footstool.
4 by one offering he has perfected 4 ever ’em dat r sanctified.
Whereof tha Holy Ghost also is a witness 2 us: 4 after dat he had said before,
Dis is tha covenant dat I will make wit ’em after dose days, says tha Lord, I will put my laws in2 their hearts, N in their minds will I write ’em;
N their sins N iniquities will I remember no more.
Now where remission of dese is, there is no more offering 4 sin.
Havin therefore, brothers, boldness 2 enter in2 tha holiest by tha blood of Jesus,
By a new N livin way, which he has consecrated 4 us, through tha veil, dat is 2 say, his flesh;
N havin an high priest over tha house of God;
Let us draw near wit a true heart in full assurance of faith, havin our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, N our bodies washed wit pure water.
Let us hold fast tha profession of our faith without wavering; (4 he is faithful dat promised;)
N let us consider one another 2 provoke 2 love N 2 good works:
Not forsaking tha assembling of ourselves together, as tha manner of some is; but exhorting one another: N so much tha more, as y’all see tha day approaching.
4 if we sin wilfully after dat we have received tha knowledge of tha truth, there remains no more sacrifice 4 sins,
But a certain fearful lookin 4 of judgment N fiery indignation, which shall devour tha adversaries.
He dat despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:

Of how much sorer punishment, suppose y’all, shall he be thought worthy, who has trodden under foot tha Son of God, N has counted tha blood of tha covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, N has done despite 2 tha Spirit of grace?
4 we know him dat has said, Vengeance belongs 2 me, I will recompense, says tha Lord. N again, tha Lord shall judge his people.
It is a fearful thing 2 fall in2 tha hands of tha livin God.
But call 2 remembrance tha former days, in which, after y’all were illuminated, y’all endured a great fight of afflictions;
Partly, whilst y’all were made a gazingstock both by reproaches N afflictions; N partly, whilst y’all became companions of ’em dat were so used.
4 y’all had compassion of me in my bonds, N took joyfully tha spoiling of ur goods, knowin in y’all dat y’all have in heaven a better N an endurin substance.
Cast not away therefore ur confidence, which has great recompence of reward.
4 y’all have need of patience, dat, after y’all have done tha will of God, y’all might receive tha promise.
4 yet a little while, N he dat shall come will come, N will not tarry.
Now tha just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
But we r not of ’em who draw back 2 perdition; but of ’em dat believe 2 tha saving of tha soul.

11.text: Now faith is tha substance of things hoped 4, tha evidence of things not seen.
4 by it tha elders obtained a good report.
Through faith we understand dat tha worlds were framed by tha word of God, so dat things which r seen were not made of things which do appear.
By faith Abel offered 2 God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness dat he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: N by it he bein dead yet speaks.
By faith Enoch was translated dat he should not see death; N was not found, because God had translated him: 4 before his translation he had dis testimony, dat he pleased God.
But without faith it is impossible 2 please him: 4 he dat comes 2 God must believe dat he is, N dat he is a rewarder of ’em dat diligently seek him.

By faith Noah, bein warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved wit fear, prepared an ark 2 tha saving of his house; by tha which he condemned tha world, N became heir of tha righteousness which is by faith.
By faith Abraham, when he was called 2 go out in2 a place which he should after receive 4 an inheritance, obeyed; N he went out, not knowin where he went.
By faith he stayed in tha land of promise, as in a strange country, livin in tabernacles wit Isaac N Jacob, tha heirs wit him of tha same promise:
4 he looked 4 a city which has foundations, whose builder N maker is God.
Through faith also Sara herself received strength 2 conceive seed, N was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.
Therefore sprang there even of one, N him as good as dead, so many as tha stars of tha sky in crowd, N as tha sand which is by tha sea shore innumerable.
Dese all died in faith, not havin received tha promises, but havin seen ’em afar off, N were persuaded of ’em, N embraced ’em, N confessed dat dey were strangers N pilgrims on tha earth.
4 dey dat say such things declare plainly dat dey seek a country.
N truly, if dey had been mindful of dat country from from where dey came out, dey might have had opportunity 2 have returned.
But now dey desire a better country, dat is, an heavenly: so God is not ashamed 2 be called their God: 4 he has prepared 4 ’em a city.
By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: N he dat had received tha promises offered up his only begotten son,
Of whom it was said, dat in Isaac shall ur seed be called:
Accounting dat God was able 2 raise him up, even from tha dead; from from where also he received him in a figure.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob N Esau concerning things 2 come.
By faith Jacob, when he was a dyin, blessed both tha sons of Joseph; N worshipped, leaning upon tha top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of tha departing of tha children of Israel; N gave commandment concerning his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because dey saw he was a proper child; N dey were not afraid of tha king’s commandment.
By faith Moses, when he was come 2 years, refused 2 be called tha son of Pharaoh’s daughter;
Choosing rather 2 suffer affliction wit tha people of God, than 2 enjoy tha pleasures of sin 4 a season;
Esteeming tha reproach of Christ greater riches than tha treasures in Egypt: 4 he had respect 2 tha recompence of tha reward.
By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearin tha wrath of tha king: 4 he endured, as seein him who is invisible.
Through faith he kept tha passover, N tha sprinkling of blood, lest he dat destroyed tha firstborn should touch ’em.
By faith dey passed through tha Red sea as by dry land: which tha Egyptians assaying 2 do were drowned.
By faith tha walls of Jericho fell down, after dey were compassed about seven days.
By faith tha harlot Rahab perished not wit ’em dat believed not, when she had received tha spies wit peace.
N what shall I more say? 4 tha time would fail me 2 tell of Gedeon, N of Barak, N of Samson, N of Jephthae; of David also, N Samuel, N of tha prophets:
Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped tha mouths of lions,
Quenched tha violence of fire, escaped tha edge of tha sword, out of weakness were made strong, grew valiant in fight, turned 2 flight tha armies of tha aliens.
Women received their dead raised 2 life again: N others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; dat dey might obtain a better resurrection:
N others had trial of cruel mockings N scourgings, yeah, moreover of bonds N imprisonment:
Dey were stoned, dey were sawn asunder, were tempted, were killed wit tha sword: dey wandered about in sheepskins N goatskins; bein destitute, afflicted, tormented;
(Of whom tha world was not worthy:) dey wandered in deserts, N in mountains, N in dens N caves of tha earth.
N dese all, havin obtained a good report through faith, received not tha promise:
God havin provided some better thing 4 us, dat dey without us should not be made perfect.

12.text: So seein we also r compassed about wit so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, N tha sin which does so easily beset us, N let us run wit patience tha race dat is set before us,
Lookin 2 Jesus tha author N finisher of our faith; who 4 tha joy dat was set before him endured tha cross, despising tha shame, N is set down at tha right hand of tha throne of God.
4 consider him dat endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest y’all be wearied N faint in ur minds.
y’all have not yet resisted 2 blood, striving against sin.
N y’all have forgotten tha exhortation which speaks 2 u as 2 children, My son, despise not u tha chastening of tha Lord, nor faint when u r rebuked of him:
4 whom tha Lord loves he chasteneth, N scourgeth every son whom he receives.
If y’all endure chastening, God deals wit u as wit sons; 4 what son is he whom tha father chasteneth not?
But if y’all be without chastisement, whereof all r partakers, then r y’all bastards, N not sons.
Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, N we gave ’em reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection 2 tha Father of spirits, N live?
4 dey for real 4 a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he 4 our profit, dat we might be partakers of his holiness.
Now no chastening 4 tha present seems 2 be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth tha peaceable fruit of righteousness 2 ’em which r exercised by dat.
So lift up tha hands which hang down, N tha feeble knees;
N make straight paths 4 ur feet, lest dat which is lame be turned out of tha way; but let it rather be healed.
Follow peace wit all men, N holiness, without which no man shall see tha Lord:
Lookin diligently lest any man fail of tha grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble u, N by dat many be defiled;
Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who 4 one morsel of food sold his birthright.
4 y’all know how dat afterward, when he would have inherited tha blessing, he was rejected: 4 he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully wit tears.
4 y’all r not come 2 tha mount dat might be touched, N dat burned wit fire, nor 2 blackness, N darkness, N tempest,
N tha sound of a trumpet, N tha voice of words; which voice dey dat heard intreated dat tha word should not be spoken 2 ’em any more:
(4 dey could not endure dat which was commanded, N if so much as a beast touch tha mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through wit a dart:
N so terrible was tha sight, dat Moses said, I exceedingly fear N quake:)
But y’all r come 2 mount Sion, N 2 tha city of tha livin God, tha heavenly Jerusalem, N 2 an innumerable company of angels,
2 tha general assembly N church of tha firstborn, which r written in heaven, N 2 God tha Judge of all, N 2 tha spirits of just men made perfect,
N 2 Jesus tha mediator of tha new covenant, N 2 tha blood of sprinkling, dat speaks better things than dat of Abel.
See dat y’all refuse not him dat speaks. 4 if dey escaped not who refused him dat spoke on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him dat speaks from heaven:
Whose voice then shook tha earth: but now he has promised, sayin, Yet once more I shake not tha earth only, but also heaven.
N dis word, Yet once more, signifieth tha removing of dose things dat r shaken, as of things dat r made, dat dose things which cannot be shaken may remain.
So we receivin a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably wit reverence N godly fear:
4 our God is a consuming fire.

13.text: Let brotherly love continue.
Don’t be forgetful 2 entertain strangers: 4 by dat some have entertained angels unawares.
Remember ’em dat r in bonds, as bound wit ’em; N ’em which suffer adversity, as bein y’all also in tha body.
Marriage is honourable in all, N tha bed undefiled: but whoremongers N adulterers God will judge.
Let ur conversation be without covetousness; N be content wit such things as y’all have: 4 he has said, I will never leave u, nor forsake u.
So dat we may boldly say, tha Lord is my helper, N I will not fear what man shall do 2 me.
Remember ’em which have tha rule over u, who have spoken 2 u tha word of God: whose faith follow, considering tha end of their conversation.
Jesus Christ tha same yesterday, N 2 day, N 4 ever.
Don’t be carried about wit divers N strange doctrines. 4 it is a good thing dat tha heart be established wit grace; not wit meats, which have not profited ’em dat have been occupied in it.
We have an altar, whereof dey have no right 2 eat which serve tha tabernacle.
4 tha bodies of dose beasts, whose blood is brought in2 tha sanctuary by tha high priest 4 sin, r burned without tha camp.
So Jesus also, dat he might sanctify tha people wit his own blood, suffered without tha gate.
Let us go forth therefore 2 him without tha camp, bearin his reproach.
4 here have we no continuing city, but we seek one 2 come.
By him therefore let us offer tha sacrifice of praise 2 God continually, dat is, tha fruit of our lips givin thanks 2 his name.
But 2 do good N 2 communicate forget not: 4 wit such sacrifices God is well pleased.
Obey ’em dat have tha rule over u, N submit y’all: 4 dey watch 4 ur souls, as dey dat must give account, dat dey may do it wit joy, N not wit grief: 4 dat is unprofitable 4 u.
Pray 4 us: 4 we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willin 2 live honestly.
But I beg u tha rather 2 do dis, dat I may be restored 2 u tha sooner.
Now tha God of peace, dat brought again from tha dead our Lord Jesus, dat great shepherd of tha sheep, through tha blood of tha everlasting covenant,
Make u perfect in every good work 2 do his will, workin in u dat which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; 2 whom be glory 4 ever N ever. Amen.
N I beg u, brothers, suffer tha word of exhortation: 4 I have written a letter 2 u in few words.
Know y’all dat our brother Timothy is set at liberty; wit whom, if he come shortly, I will see u.
Greet all ’em dat have tha rule over u, N all tha saints. dey of Italy greet u.
Grace be wit u all. Amen.
